idiom_name: enum event + serde internally-tagged representation; tokio broadcast or a broker client
implementation_notes: A Rust enum is a closed, immutable sum type, and serde's internally tagged representation (#[serde(tag = "type")]) makes the variant name the wire discriminator - the classic hand-written envelope plus type switch is replaced by the derive macro, and match on the enum replaces virtual dispatch with compiler-checked exhaustiveness. In-process fan-out is tokio::sync::broadcast, where each Receiver gets its own clone of every value and lag is reported rather than hidden; cross-process delivery uses a broker client (rdkafka, lapin, async-nats) with the same enum as the payload type. There is no idiomatic Rust event class hierarchy: enums plus serde are the replacement, and the compiler enforces that every new event variant is handled everywhere it must be.
pitfalls: Internally tagged enums cannot contain tuple variants - a compile error, not a silent bug; use struct variants or adjacent tagging (tag + content) instead.
A broadcast receiver that falls behind returns RecvError::Lagged and messages are dropped: it is a fan-out channel, not a durable queue, so persist events elsewhere when loss is unacceptable.
An enum's size is its largest variant; box a fat variant or hold ids to keep the channel buffer cheap.
Unknown or renamed event types fail deserialisation unless the contract stays additive and consumers use #[serde(other)]-style fallbacks (tolerant reader).
